reading.a: A large orange sun sits behind a two-level road bridge at dusk: a thin dark powerline crosses the sky and the sun about 100 px above the deck (rows 149-175, falling slightly to the right), the dark deck (element 16) and the truss under it (element 29), and an orange reflection column on dark water.
reading.b: The Andromeda galaxy: an orange core at (960, 521) in a disk tilted down to the right, a dark dust lane below-left of the core, a star field, and one straight satellite streak at about -19 degrees passing 60 px below the core.

concepts.idea: The camera pulls back as in rounds 8 and 9 while, in this order, the brightest stars come through the red sky first (from t 0.08), the powerline swings 19 degrees and stretches into the satellite streak as a thin line (t 0.12-0.70), the sun falls away into the core with its rim melting into the core's glow from the first frame of the recede (t 0.15-0.90), the whole bridge, deck and truss with soft edges, folds into the galaxy's dusty arm with only the bridge moving in depth (t 0.20-0.85), the sky gives way to space in the slow wide crossfade (t 0.25-0.92), and the core takes over the last of the sun brightest-first (t 0.72-1.0).

anchors.how: Unchanged from rounds 8 and 9: the sun's fitted centre (about (994, 102), radius about 275 px) lands on the measured core centre; at end_scale 0.4 the sun is 110 px, the glow's half-maximum radius.
Unchanged from round 9: the powerline (row 149 at the left edge, 165 in the middle, 175 at the right edge) is A's one thin dark straight line; the streak is B's one thin bright straight line.
Unchanged from round 9: deck and truss together are the bridge's dark mass; the dust lane is the darkest wide band under the core.

transforms.name: sun_recedes
transforms.note: Beat 1, the sun falls away into the core, unchanged in path and size. Answers 'still some hard edges around sun' (his frame: a bright ring and a dark gap at the rim): the limb mixes into the core's glow from the recede's first frame (mix_window [0.0, 0.95]) over the wide ramp 0.6, and limb_flatten 1.0 keeps the paler inner disc that drew the ring out.

transforms.name: wire_to_streak
transforms.note: Beat 2, his idea of round 8 ('barely visible thin powerline ... transformed into that diagonal streak'), unchanged window. Answers the wire's 'tilted bar' in his round-9 frame: the band's alpha is now the wire's own darkness (the round-10 dark_line rule), so the 7-row band carries the line and not the sky around it; end_taper 0 says so explicitly.

transforms.name: bridge_to_arm
transforms.note: Beat 3, kept ('bridge trasforms into arm , nice', round 8). Answers 'hard edges around ... bridge' (the deck as a hard-edged bar with a grey band, and the vertical bands above the lamp posts): elements 16 and 29 now composite with their soft mattes, A's plate fills under them, and pullback.parallax.a_elements [16, 29] confines the depth remap to the bridge so no sky pixel is remapped.

knobs.name: sun_recedes.params.mix_ramp
knobs.what: How wide the limb-first mix of the sun into the core's glow is; wider leaves less of a rim at any moment.

knobs.name: parallax_A_elements
knobs.what: The A elements the depth parallax acts on; an empty list turns A's parallax off entirely if the bridge's own remap still tears its edge.

knobs.name: container.params.sky.key_band
knobs.what: How wide the sky's luma crossfade band is; raise it if the red sky still leaves a luma border at the disc now that the early colour lead is gone.

concepts.risk: F1 double exposure: the sky_colour_leads transform of round 9 is dropped to meet the three-transform rule, so the slow key now crosses an undarkened red sky; watch t 0.3-0.6 for a red-to-black luma border around the receding sun (the knob is key_band). The wire crosses the sun disc at x about 800-1190, so the recede layer and the line_to band both carry its pixels there; a dark chord on the sun during t 0.15-0.4 is that. F2 decoration: if the bridge's soft matte is wider than the deck, the plate's fill shows as a blurred band along the deck's top edge (the grey band of round 9 in another form). F3 invention: none expected; every star is B's, the plate is a fill of A's own pixels.
